notes: Pandu's line ruled Anuradhapura c. 429-455. Kiribamune: 5th-century inscriptions show these Tamil rulers had Buddhist leanings; Khudda Parinda's queen endowed a Buddhist monastery. Conquerors' prior religion undocumented, Hindu by inference only.

Judaism gained a firm foothold in Himyar from the late 4th century; Dhu Nuwas massacred Najran Christians (520). Aksum, officially Christian since Ezana, crushed Himyar in 525; Abraha, a zealous Christian, massacred Jews and built a Sanaa church.

source2: Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Bukhara ii. From the Arab invasions to the Mongols' - https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/bukhara-ii
notes: Satuq Bughra Khan (d. c. 955) was the first Muslim Qarakhanid; mass Turkic conversion followed in 960. Ilak Nasr definitively occupied Samanid Bukhara in 999. Qarakhanid coins bore Arabic and Uighur scripts.

Kalachuri Bijjala usurped Kalyani c. 1156; his reign saw the Hindu Lingayat sect emerge, though Kalachuri kings patronized Jainism. Chalukya rule was restored under Someshvara IV. Chalukyas' Hindu identity is standard but not explicit in opened pages.
